faq.question: Is Melbourne really the coffee capital of Australia?
faq.answer: Yes, by most measures. Melbourne is widely regarded as one of the world's top three coffee cities alongside Tokyo and Oslo. The city mainstreamed the flat white globally, developed the Magic (a Melbourne-original drink), and has had a sophisticated specialty coffee culture for decades before the global third wave.

faq.question: What is a flat white?
faq.answer: A flat white is a Melbourne original — espresso topped with microfoam (silky steamed milk with minimal froth), creating a stronger, smaller drink than a latte. Typically served in a ceramic cup, never paper. The flat white spread globally from Melbourne and Sydney in the 2000s and is now on Starbucks menus worldwide.

faq.question: What is a Magic coffee?
faq.answer: The Magic is a Melbourne invention — a double ristretto (shorter, more concentrated espresso) served in a smaller cup (typically 160ml) with silky steamed milk. It's stronger than a flat white, more intense, and rarely found outside Melbourne and Australian specialty cafes.

faq.question: How much does specialty coffee cost in Melbourne?
faq.answer: Specialty espresso drinks in Melbourne cost AU$4.50–$7. A flat white or latte is typically AU$4.50–$5.50. Filter coffee (pour-over or batch brew) is AU$5–$8. Melbourne coffee is consistently cheaper than equivalent quality in London or New York.

faq.question: Which Melbourne suburb has the best coffee?
faq.answer: Fitzroy and Collingwood have the highest concentration of excellent specialty cafes. The CBD laneways (Little Bourke Street, Flinders Lane) have world-class options within walking distance. North Melbourne and Brunswick are also excellent for specialty coffee with more local neighbourhood vibes.

methodology: We analyzed 90+ Reddit posts across r/Melbourne, r/Coffee, r/AusFood, and specialty coffee forums — spanning 2020 to 2026. Cafes ranked by recommendation frequency from users who know their coffee.
